nodes.description: A direct connection forms between an artery and a vein with no intervening capillary bed. nodes.description: Two endothelial-cell-autonomous defects follow. First, endothelial cells normally polarise against the direction of blood flow and migrate upstream; without ALK1 signalling that shear-directed migration is lost and the cells stall. Second, the stalled cells keep proliferating - in part because BMP9/10 signalling normally restrains PI3K/AKT, so its loss increases endothelial proliferation and survival. The pathway also normally damps endothelial responses to VEGF, which is why anti-VEGF therapy is effective downstream. In adult vessels this only becomes visible when an angiogenic trigger is present. Two mechanisms have been resolved for how the brake is applied. ALK1-driven SMAD signalling cooperates with Notch in stalk cells to induce HEY1 and HEY2, which repress VEGF signalling, tip-cell formation and sprouting - so blocking Alk1 gives retinal hypervascularisation and AVMs, and activating it with BMP9 rescues hypersprouting caused by Notch inhibition. Separately, the pathway sets the fluid-shear-stress set point at which endothelium is stable; losing the downstream node SMAD4 lowers that set point and disinhibits flow-driven KLF4-TIE2-PI3K/Akt signalling, so cells proliferate and lose arterial identity under flow that would otherwise be quiescent.

nodes.description: Arteriovenous malformations arising within the brain or spinal cord itself, distinct from the embolic cerebral complications of a pulmonary shunt. nodes.description: Oral immunomodulatory agent for refractory epistaxis and gastrointestinal bleeding. In a randomised placebo-controlled trial it reduced the Epistaxis Severity Score by 0.94 points more than placebo - above the 0.71-point threshold considered clinically significant - with neutropenia, constipation and rash as the excess adverse events. The trial was stopped early at a planned interim analysis for efficacy. It was not stratified by genotype, but a post-hoc response analysis found ACVRL1 germline mutation among the characteristics associated with a *less* robust response (+0.62 ESS points versus ENG, SMAD4 or unknown genotype). That is a trend at P=0.06, not a result - but it is the first genotype signal for treatment stratification in HHT, and it points the wrong way for this entity, so it is recorded here rather than left in the trial literature. An open-label extension followed 62 patients for up to 4.4 years and found the epistaxis benefit durable, while noting that pomalidomide was less effective for gastrointestinal bleeding - the bleeding compartment that is disproportionately HHT2's.

nodes.description: Pregnancy is not a cause of HHT2 but is its best-characterised physiological trigger. The peripheral vasodilation and rise in cardiac output of pregnancy load an already-shunting circulation, and adverse events reported in HHT pregnancies include heart failure, pulmonary and intracranial haemorrhage, and stroke. This is why the guidelines screen and treat pulmonary and cerebral AVMs before or during pregnancy, and why sizable pulmonary AVMs found in pregnancy are treated in the second trimester. Complications cluster in the second and third trimesters, when the maternal haemodynamic changes are maximal.

nodes.description: Pre-capillary pulmonary arterial hypertension from obliterative remodelling of small pulmonary arteries, clinically and histologically indistinguishable from idiopathic PAH. Among the HHT genes this is best established for ACVRL1, and it is mechanistically distinct from - though it can coexist with - the post-capillary pressure elevation of a high-output hepatic shunt. A figure of about 20% of ACVRL1-associated HHT patients developing PAH is in circulation; the citable statement of it available here is a background sentence in a case report, itself citing a further source, so the number is reported with that provenance rather than used to set a frequency band.

Present in HHT2 but much less often than in HHT1 - 5.2% symptomatic in the French-Italian cohort and 24.4% on screening in the Spanish registry, against 34.4% and 71.4% respectively for HHT1. Screening is still indicated in ACVRL1 carriers because the complications are abrupt.

evidence.reference_title: Genotype-phenotype correlations in hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia: data from the French-Italian HHT network.
evidence.snippet: Symptomatic PAVMs were more frequent in HHT1 (34.4 vs. 5.2%, P<0.001), as were cerebral abscesses (7.5 vs. 0.8%, P=0.002).

evidence.reference_title: Current HHT genetic overview in Spain and its phenotypic correlation: data from RiHHTa registry.
evidence.snippet: ENG patients were significantly younger at diagnosis (36.9 vs 45.7 years) and had pulmonary arteriovenous malformations (AVMs) (71.4% vs 24.4%) and cerebral AVMs (17.6% vs 2%) more often than patients with ACVRL1 variants.

nodes.description: Pulmonary AVMs connect a pulmonary artery to a pulmonary vein, so venous blood bypasses the alveolar capillary bed and enters the systemic circulation unfiltered and incompletely oxygenated. Pulmonary AVMs occur in HHT2 but are markedly less frequent than in HHT1 - about 5% versus 34% for symptomatic lesions in the French-Italian cohort. That lower frequency does not remove the need for screening, because the consequences of an unscreened lesion are catastrophic rather than gradual.

evidence.reference_title: Genotype-phenotype correlations in hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia: data from the French-Italian HHT network.
evidence.snippet: Symptomatic PAVMs were more frequent in HHT1 (34.4 vs. 5.2%, P<0.001), as were cerebral abscesses (7.5 vs. 0.8%, P=0.002).

evidence.reference_title: Current HHT genetic overview in Spain and its phenotypic correlation: data from RiHHTa registry.
evidence.snippet: ENG patients were significantly younger at diagnosis (36.9 vs 45.7 years) and had pulmonary arteriovenous malformations (AVMs) (71.4% vs 24.4%) and cerebral AVMs (17.6% vs 2%) more often than patients with ACVRL1 variants.

nodes.description: Recurrent spontaneous nosebleeds from ruptured nasal mucosal telangiectases; the cardinal and usually earliest manifestation of HHT, and the first Curacao criterion. In HHT2 it begins later than in HHT1 and is incompletely penetrant, so its absence in a young ACVRL1 carrier does not exclude the diagnosis. No frequency is recorded here because the HHT2-specific sources report incomplete penetrance without a percentage.

evidence.reference_title: Hereditary Hemorrhagic Telangiectasia.
evidence.snippet: The most common clinical manifestation is recurrent nosebleeds (epistaxis) beginning on average at age 12 years.

evidence.reference_title: Genotype-phenotype correlations in hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia: data from the French-Italian HHT network.
evidence.snippet: Epistaxis occurred later in HHT2, with incomplete penetrance (P<0.0001).

evidence.reference_title: Genotype-phenotype correlation in hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia: mutations and manifestations.
evidence.snippet: We found that epistaxis had an earlier onset in patients with HHT1 than those with HHT2, but the severity by middle ages was similar.

nodes.description: ALK1 is the type I receptor for the circulating ligands BMP9 and BMP10. Ligand is captured by the co-receptor endoglin and handed to ALK1, a type II receptor joins and phosphorylates ALK1, and activated ALK1 phosphorylates SMAD1/5. With less functional ALK1, flux through this specific BMP9/10-ENG-ALK1 arm falls. Mouse work indicates BMP10 rather than BMP9 is the ligand whose loss reproduces the AVM phenotype.

evidence.reference_title: BMP10 functions independently from BMP9 for the development of a proper arteriovenous network.
evidence.snippet: We suggest that BMP10 is the most relevant physiological ligand of the ENG-ALK1 signaling pathway pertinent to HHT pathogenesis.

evidence.reference_title: BMP10 functions independently from BMP9 for the development of a proper arteriovenous network.
evidence.snippet: Bmp10-iKO and Bmp9/10-dKO mice showed AVMs in developing retina, postnatal brain, and adult wounded skin, while Bmp9-KO did not display any noticeable vascular defects.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical and molecular genetic features of pulmonary hypertension in patients with hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia.
evidence.snippet: Immunohistochemical analysis in four subjects and one control showed pulmonary vascular endothelial expression of activin-receptor-like kinase 1 in normal and diseased pulmonary arteries.

molecular_functions: ALK1 type I receptor serine/threonine kinase activity

nodes.description: Individual lesions acquire a somatic mutation in the remaining wild-type ACVRL1 allele, producing local biallelic loss. This is what reconciles a germline variant present in every endothelial cell with a disease that is focal: telangiectases and AVMs arise where a second hit has occurred, not everywhere. Lesion-specific somatic ACVRL1 variants have been recovered from hepatic AVMs and from a skin telangiectasia in a patient whose germline lesion was a whole-gene ACVRL1 deletion, with different somatic variants in different lesions of the same person.
nodes.id: Somatic Second-Hit Inactivation of the Remaining ACVRL1 Allele

evidence.reference_title: Multiple lesion-specific somatic mutations and bi-allelic loss of ACVRL1 in a single patient with hereditary haemorrhagic telangiectasia.
evidence.snippet: Somatic mosaic lesion-specific ACVRL1 variants were identified in four hepatic AVM samples and in one telangiectasia.

evidence.reference_title: An update on preclinical models of hereditary haemorrhagic telangiectasia: Insights into disease mechanisms.
evidence.snippet: Increasing evidence points to the importance of a second genetic hit to generate biallelic mutations, and the sporadic nature of such somatic mutations would explain the localised formation of vascular lesions.

nodes.description: Spinal arteriovenous malformation. Reported as an HHT2-selective lesion: in a US cohort of 111 patients from 34 families, spinal AVMs were seen only in HHT2. This is a single-cohort observation and should be read as a signal rather than a settled genotype restriction.

evidence.reference_title: Genotype-phenotype correlation in hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia: mutations and manifestations.
evidence.snippet: Cerebral arteriovenous malformations were more common in patients with HHT1, but spinal arteriovenous malformations were seen only in patients with HHT2.

nodes.description: Intravenous anti-VEGF monoclonal antibody. The most HHT2-relevant systemic therapy: in a phase II trial of patients with severe hepatic vascular malformations and high cardiac output, bevacizumab lowered cardiac index in 20 of 24 patients and also reduced epistaxis duration. Before this, liver transplantation was the only way to restore cardiac output in these patients. It works upstream of the bleeding, on the excess VEGF-driven angiogenic drive released by loss of ALK1 signalling, rather than on haemostasis.

evidence.reference_title: Bevacizumab in patients with hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia and severe hepatic vascular malformations and high cardiac output.
evidence.snippet: In this preliminary study of patients with HHT associated with severe hepatic vascular malformations and high cardiac output, administration of bevacizumab was associated with a decrease in cardiac output and reduced duration and number of episodes of epistaxis.

evidence.reference_title: Bevacizumab in patients with hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia and severe hepatic vascular malformations and high cardiac output.
evidence.snippet: The most severe adverse events were 2 cases of grade 3 systemic hypertension, which were successfully treated.

nodes.description: Oral antiangiogenic used for HHT-associated bleeding, described as acting by bolstering blood-vessel maturation rather than by blocking VEGF outright. The third of the three established angiogenesis inhibitors in HHT practice.

evidence.reference_title: Systemic Antiangiogenic Therapies for Bleeding in Hereditary Hemorrhagic Telangiectasia: A Practical, Evidence-Based Guide for Clinicians.
evidence.snippet: Intravenous bevacizumab, oral pazopanib, and oral thalidomide are the three targeted primary angiogenesis inhibitors, with multiple studies describing both reassuring safety and impressive effectiveness in the treatment of moderate-to-severe HHT-associated bleeding.

evidence.reference_title: Hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia and pregnancy: potential adverse events and pregnancy outcomes.
evidence.snippet: bevacizumab and pazopanib inhibit angiogenesis, while thalidomide bolsters blood vessel maturation

nodes.description: Oral antifibrinolytic used first-line for epistaxis and gastrointestinal bleeding. It acts on the consequence of the lesions - haemostasis at the bleeding site - and not on the vascular malformation itself.

evidence.reference_title: Hereditary Hemorrhagic Telangiectasia.
evidence.snippet: Oral tranexamic acid or intravenous bevacizumab for epistaxis and GI bleeding; pomalidomide or pazopanib for refractory epistaxis and GI bleeding.

nodes.description: Occlusion of pulmonary AVMs with a feeding vessel of 2-3 mm or greater, done for stroke prevention rather than for symptoms. This is prophylaxis against the paradoxical-embolism pathway, and it remains indicated in HHT2 despite the lower lesion frequency.
nodes.id: Transcatheter Embolization of Pulmonary Arteriovenous Malformations

evidence.reference_title: Hereditary Hemorrhagic Telangiectasia.
evidence.snippet: Pulmonary AVMs with a feeding vessel 2-3 mm or greater in diameter typically require occlusion for stroke prevention.

nodes.description: Nonsense and frameshift variants predicted to abolish receptor function. Within HHT2 they are associated with a higher frequency of epistaxis and telangiectasis than non-truncating variants.

evidence.reference_title: Genotype-phenotype correlations in hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia: data from the French-Italian HHT network.
evidence.snippet: Truncating mutations were associated with a higher frequency of epistaxis and telangiectasis, in HHT2.
